title: Rework quiet-affordance icon button and microstate transitions
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Problem: Icon-only buttons that use the current 'ghost' styling experience multiple regressions across themes and densities. We see focus ring loss when switching to a loading spinner, layout shifts when icons are swapped for spinners, inconsistent spinner coloration in dark/high-contrast themes, and non-deterministic hit-target sizes when text-labels are absent. This ticket scopes a new 'quiet-affordance' icon-button variant plus an animation/microstate strategy that preserves focus, prevents layout shift, respects reduced-motion, and standardizes token usage across themes.

Goals:
- Introduce a new variant named 'quiet-affordance' (icon-only, minimal surface) that explicitly reserves space for transient states (spinner, checkmark) to avoid layout shift.
- Define microstate transitions (idle -> pending -> success/error -> idle) with focus-preserving animations and interruptible loading behavior.
- Ensure spinner and glyph colors follow tokens per theme and support high-contrast override.
- Provide clear token contract for designers and engineers (sizes, padding, spinner slot, focus ring offset).
- Add visual regression tests, keyboard/accessibility tests, and QA playbook for edge cases (RTL, density changes, motion disabled).
acceptance_criteria: New 'quiet-affordance' variant available in Figma and component library
No layout shift when toggling loading state across all density tokens
Keyboard focus preserved and visible through pending state (meets WCAG 2.2 focus contrast guidance)
Spinner color driven by theme tokens and matches contrast targets in light/dark/high-contrast
Reduced-motion users see an immediate state change without non-essential animation
Unit + visual tests added to component storybook and CI, and test matrix covers core themes
decisions: Use a fixed-size inner content box for icon buttons (24px logical) with center-aligned glyph and reserved spinner slot
Spinner overlays are preferred to swapping DOM nodes; use opacity/scale transitions to avoid reflow
Focus ring rendered outside reserved content box using tokenized offset so ring persists during content opacity transitions
Token names: token.button.icon.quiet.size, token.button.icon.quiet.padding, token.button.icon.quiet.spinner-color, token.button.icon.quiet.focus-offset
Loading can be cancelable via an exposed 'cancelLoading' callback; engineering to design API shape with retries/fallbacks
tradeoffs_and_risks: Fixed-size content box slightly reduces flexibility for very large custom icons; tradeoff intentional for layout stability
Overlay spinner adds one extra DOM layer; minor perf cost but avoids relayout and visual jitter
Introducing new variant increases surface area for tokens; requires careful token mapping to prevent duplication across existing variants
Backward compatibility: existing 'ghost' variant behavior preserved; migration guide required for teams wanting the new stable behavior
design_notes: Figma component uses Auto Layout with a 24px content frame, 8px outer padding tokenized; sprite icons must align to the 24px grid
Microstate animation timeline: pending fade-in 120ms (opacity + scale 0.92->1), success checkmark crossfade 80ms, error shake reduced-motion fallback immediate
Focus ring uses a 3px tokenized offset so that inner opacity transitions do not obscure the ring
We will provide two spinner sizes (small/medium) but small is the default for icon-only buttons
Provide explicit ARIA guidance: aria-busy on the button during pending, aria-live region only for persistent status messages, and ensure role='button' and focusable attribute preserved
